title: Conditional information under duality
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and $p$ a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set. Let $X,X'$ be Boolean-valued functions on the hard-sample space, and let $Z,Z'$ be functions from that space to a special coordinate together with two Boolean vectors. Suppose for every hard sample $\omega$ that $X'$ evaluated on the dual sample equals $X(\omega)$, and that $Z'$ evaluated on the dual sample equals the coordinate-reversed and party-swapped recoding of $Z(\omega)$. Then, under the hard-sample distribution conditioned on disjoint inputs, the conditional mutual information between $X'$ and the transcript of the dual protocol given $Z'$ equals the conditional mutual information between $X$ and the transcript of $p$ given $Z$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol on pairs of subsets of an $n$-element coordinate set
$X,X'$ are Boolean-valued functions on the hard-sample space
$Z,Z'$ take values in a special coordinate and two Boolean vectors
For every sample, $X'$ on its dual equals $X$ on the original sample
For every sample, $Z'$ on its dual equals the dual recoding of $Z$ on the original sample
replaced:
Let $p$ be a protocol on the hard sample space, let $X, X' : \Omega \to \{0,1\}$ be two
Boolean variables and let $Z, Z' : \Omega \to [n] \times \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ be two
conditioning variables on the hard sample $\Omega = \texttt{HardSample}\,n$.  Suppose that
$X'$ and $Z'$ evaluated on the dual sample are $X$ and the recoded $Z$ on the original
sample, i.e.\ $X'(\sigma(\omega)) = X(\omega)$ and
$Z'(\sigma(\omega)) = \delta(Z(\omega))$ for every $\omega$, where $\sigma$ is the
hard-sample duality \texttt{dualHardSample} and $\delta$ the conditioning recoding
\texttt{dualConditioningValue}.  Then, under the disjoint-conditioned measure $\mu_{\mathcal D}$,
the conditional mutual information between $X'$ and the transcript of the dual protocol
$\bar p$ given $Z'$ equals that between $X$ and the transcript of $p$ given $Z$:
\[
  I\bigl[X' : M_{\bar p} \mid Z' ;\ \mu_{\mathcal D}\bigr]
  \;=\;
  I\bigl[X : M_{p} \mid Z ;\ \mu_{\mathcal D}\bigr],
\]
where $M_p = \texttt{message}\,n\,p$ denotes the transcript of $p$.
